## Procedure

1. **Read the artifact cold**, plus any docs that embed or describe it.
2. **Classify against the existing ontology, in three confidence tiers** —
   report all three explicitly. **Verify candidates against the source
   tables by FULL name, never by name fragments** — a fragment query
   misses template instances and long-form names, and a wrong
   "nothing defines this" claim has minted a redundant stub over an
   existing template. When claiming absence, read the table.
   - **Tier 1, mechanical** (would auto-propose): exact column-header matches
     to existing catalogs; cell values resolving to existing node names
     (through aliases); edge shapes already in the vocabulary.
   - **Tier 2, observations** (flag, don't act): near-matches, sibling
     patterns, sentinel values, terminology drift.
   - **Tier 3, genuine owner questions** (the 20%): concept classification,
     facet membership, naming, modeling choices, and **missing engine
     primitives a second consumer already wants** (see the missing-primitive
     rule in Cautions). Never answer these yourself.
3. **Read the facet checklist from the graph**, not from memory:
   instances of the `Facet` archetype (with `doc` explanations). Ask of the
   new concept: ordered? exclusive? stateful? — one question per facet.
   **For every ordered ladder, establish its DIRECTION** (owner rule):
   ascending, descending, or neither — deduce it from the artifact's own
   mechanics where possible, and where it is not clear to deduce, ask
   the owner. Record the answer where the ladder is declared. Rules
   prose saying "above/higher" over a ladder whose direction was never
   pinned is exactly how opposite readings of the same sentence survive
   into play.
4. **Resolve Tier 3 by scenario interview**: pose concrete situations
   from the corpus's own world, engineered so different answers imply
   different classifications. Expect the owner to redirect to
   prose — read the cited docs and come back with findings. Expect judgments
   to flip; that's the process working.

   **The interview is ONE collated question sheet — never a stream.**
   Serial questioning — one ping at a time, context scattered across
   messages, the owner put on the spot — is not a permitted interview
   shape, however urgent a single question feels. Instead: finish the
   recon, compose EVERY owner question, then present them together as
   one sheet the owner reads at their own pace and answers in any
   order. On the sheet, each question is BUILT with its context, not
   dressed at presentation: the evidence quoted verbatim (the
   artifact's sentences, the graph record's own text — each labeled
   with where it lives), the tension between them named explicitly,
   what each answer would do, and a recommendation. A question the
   owner cannot rule on from its entry alone is not ready for the
   sheet — hold it and gather the missing context first. Follow-ups
   spawned by an answer join the NEXT collated sheet (or the diff
   gate), never an immediate counter-question; after a rejected or
   challenged sheet, the next message is evidence and prose only.
   (This mirrors the convergence loop's one-collated-escalation-gate —
   the shape that has never drawn a complaint. agentic-intake's
   gate-voice self-check enforces the same rules at presentation time;
   the discipline starts here, where the questions are made.)
5. **Prose rule (two-stage, protects ETL determinism)**: never have the build
   interpret prose. Extract a structured proposal (table/YAML) from prose
   NOW, with the owner; the approver approves it; the approved artifact
   is kept in the project's history; the deterministic ETL consumes only that. Mark all extracted
   content as REQUIRING DESIGNER REVIEW.
6. **File findings as issues** (issue-first convention): data problems,
   terminology drift, rules gaps — one issue per finding class, presenting
   options without deciding them.
7. **Implement only after the owner rules**: the schema lands through
   the schema ceremony — a label birth or concept declaration in a
   gated round (the spec: concept list, ordered flag, catalog,
   properties, relationships — with `on_missing: placeholder` for
   name-like columns, `report` + `unmatched_property` for prose-like
   columns). Then the maintenance loop
   (see the rebuild-graph skill): rederive where a ceremony moved the
   schema (the backup re-export rides it; golden in the same change
   set) → test → restore scratch → MCP verify.
8. **Record what was deferred**: every corpus records deferred
   machinery explicitly as a Judgment row (e.g. "TRANSITIONS_TO awaits docs spike").
9. **The glossary stage**: run `python -m graph terms` after mapping. New
   citizens often resolve old unresolved terms; whatever remains gets
   classified (surface form/alias | stub concept | pending_instance |
   reject), never silenced. When a mapped label absorbs a stub concept's
   territory, graduate its pending_instances into real rows and delete the
   stub — the worklist (`MATCH (s:Archetype {stub: true})`) should shrink
   with every intake.

## 7. Evaluability: traces, the run graph, and the regression corpus

[operator FATAL: no run-trace; historian FATAL: no way to show any
future version is better; refuter: four author claims in v1's own
evidence appendix were untraceable to the record — confirmed]

- **Every run emits a trace**: who was cast, what they were told, what
  they cited, what the judge ruled, what escalated. Claims about runs
  cite traces; recollection is not a source.
- **The trace is a run-scoped judgment graph** [owner]: Question /
  Answer / Decision nodes with decided_by: <agent>, scoped to the run,
  archived beside it at run end (inspectable forever, canon never) and
  discarded from the working set. Precedent: the judging machinery's
  per-artifact workspace database. Agent judgments are OPINIONS with
  confidence (made a kernel class) until the owner ratifies one — ratification
  promotes it to a durable, owner-authority Judgment row through the
  normal ceremony. Born ephemeral, promoted by ruling. Implemented:
  graph/runs.py — pure-logic build, JSONL archive under
  graph/runs/<run-id>/, and a promotion helper whose package cites the
  run id and nothing archive-internal (canon survives archive loss).
  Span anchors implemented: judgments carry (artifact
  fingerprint, start, end, quoted text) — the quote re-locates the
  span when the artifact moves; margin() reads an artifact's anchored
  judgments in span order and render_margin presents them in place;
  archiving with artifact bytes refuses quotes that are not there.
- **Canon attribution closes the triangle** (owner-ruled): parity
  proves draft ≡ original; attribution
  (graph/attribution.py, wired into the roundtrip scorecard and the
  whole-book unit `roundtrip --book`) proves draft ⊆ canon on a graded
  source ladder — structured properties, carried receipts, long-prose
  homes (the soup rung, attributed AND a named debt). A homeless claim
  splits on parity: original says it → CANON GAP (auto-debt, shipping
  never stops at any density); parity called it invented →
  UNATTRIBUTED INVENTION (presented with the artifact, named red,
  never hidden). Citations are strong-form: earned only when the
  cited citizen is in the drafter's trace-recorded consulted set;
  unearned-but-correct re-derives invisibly. Inputs are layered: the
  original and any finding quoting it are evaluator-internal;
  generator feedback is redacted to defect-class + citizen pointers.
  The original remains the parity reference until the owner EXPLICITLY
  declares succession — no milestone implies it. Attribution and
  ingestion are one mapping machinery in two directions; intake runs
  sealed-then-mapping (the pocket-universe phasing; the visibility
  system that will enforce the seal physically is designed and built
  at [lenses.md](lenses.md) — the seal rides as discipline
  until the declarations take graph residence at the owner's gate).
- **The regression corpus**: owner-approved floors are re-checked
  before any "done" — a fix cannot silently break prior approvals, and
  the second occurrence of a defect class is caught before the owner
  sees it. First-of-class remains the owner's catch, honestly.
  Implemented: graph/corpus.py + the committed ledger
  graph/corpus/floors.jsonl — one floor per approval (guard test node,
  scope, expectation in plain words, provenance), `python -m graph
  corpus` re-checks all of them, and a deleted or renamed guard reds
  as "the guard is gone" naming the approval it orphaned.
- Critique panels police themselves: mixed framing (not all
  refutation), inter-rater agreement recorded in the trace, unanimity
  flagged as suspicious rather than celebrated. [historian, applied to
  the very panel that reviewed this document]

## Glossary, the working vocabulary

*The hardcore definitions — the lay glossary above stays the
gentle entry point. A knowledge base's own domain terms are
not here: they live on the graph itself
(`python -m graph terms`; every citizen carries its own doc)
and in the consuming project's own glossary.*

### The one people ask about first

**Floor** — a promise already made. Two braided uses. The **honest
floor** is the named list of everything still imperfect when work is
presented: remaining defects are classified and shown *with* the work,
never hidden under it — "an honest red beats a faked green." A
**corpus floor** is one owner-approved expectation made durable: the
check that guards it, the expectation in plain words, and the approval
that made it a floor (a PR, a ruling), re-checked by `python -m graph
corpus` before any "done." Work may build *above* a floor; it may
never sink below one, and a floor whose guard vanishes is a loud red,
never a silence.

### Canon and the graph

**Canon** — the Neo4j canon database: the single source of truth
for everything the knowledge base asserts. Files are inputs and backups;
the graph is primary.

**Citizen** — any node that lives in canon. Facts, rulings, procedures,
quotes — if it matters, it's a citizen, queryable and owned.

**Backup / export** — `graph/export/*.jsonl`, written FROM canon,
kept under whatever custody the knowledge base uses (this project
keeps them in git). `restore` rebuilds the database from it alone.

**The drill** — restore from backup, then prove the database
re-serializes byte-identical. Run constantly; "DRILL PASSED" is canon's
heartbeat.

**Ground vs. machine layer** — ground facts are authored (by people or
gated rounds); the machine layer (Archetype nodes, derived edges like
INSTANCE_OF) is *computed* from ground + schema at every apply. Nobody
authors the machine layer; re-derivation owns it.

**Receipts** — review-evidence properties on authored citizens
(`from_text`, `source`, `grade`): the verbatim quote and provenance
that let a claim be checked. Never rendered into outputs.

### The two schema layers

**Metaontology (the kernel)** — the engine's own vocabulary
(`graph/metaontology.yaml`): the four roots (Concept, Facet,
Provenance, Judgment), [Procedure], the Judgment family, the
visibility vocabulary, the artifact family ([Artifact], its
location and interpretation machinery), and the worlds vocabulary
([Knowledge Base Dependency], [Citizen Bookmark], [Pocket
Universe]). Project-agnostic — the membership test is "would a kid's
storybook project need it?" Semver'd; changes are **ceremonies**.

**Project ontology** — everything THIS knowledge base holds as its own
schema: its labels, catalogs, relationships — living ON the graph as
the Archetype stratum. Owner-governed, versioned as a plain revision
number. The from-sources
era is closed: every knowledge base is born graph-native, and
bootstrap files are
archaeology, kept only in the project's own history.

**Ceremony** — the deliberate act of changing the kernel: explicit
owner ruling, a Decision row naming it, the version bump and ledger
line in the same change set. Never casual, never a side effect. The
**schema ceremony** is its project-layer sibling: a closed list of
permitted change classes riding an ordinary gated round, itemized in the delta
report's marked section — approving that round IS the ruling.

**Born graph-native** — a knowledge base seeded from the kernel alone
(`python -m graph init`): no bootstrap files, no sources; its project
layer starts empty and grows through gated rounds.

**Label birth** — the schema-ceremony class that grows an empty
project layer: a new spec-carrying label arriving with its
declaration, permitted only while nothing yet sits underneath it.

### Rounds — how canon changes

**Round** — the unit of canon change: cut scratch → author → delta →
gates → apply. Nothing reaches canon any other way.

**Scratch** — a working database cloned from canon where agents author
freely. Wiped and re-cut per round; mistakes here cost nothing.

**Base pin** — cutting scratch records canon's content identity. If
canon moves mid-round, the apply refuses by name — no round lands on a
base that shifted under it.

**Branch** — an independent line of truth WITHIN a KB: born from a
declared base (schema-only for a rebuild line; clone-of-canon for a
pocket), with its own authoring
copy, ceremony, and chained log, physically unable to write the KB's
live canon, adopted only by the owner's succession ceremony — never a
flag. Pinned base + delta is the contract; the clone is an
implementation detail. A **Pocket Universe ("Pocket")** is a branch
cut as a clone of canon and declared a pocket; its work returns
through merge, prepared as the target's ordinary gated round. The
world-level correlation of pockets — one per member KB the work
mutates, read-pins for the rest, landing at one collated gate with
verify-all-before-apply-any extended across every member KB — is
the designed next rung.

**Delta / proposal** — the itemized changeset: scratch minus base,
linted (machine layers refuse authorship), rendered as a report. Its
content hash IS the proposal's identity.

**Plan gate / diff gate** — the two owner gates: the plan gate rules
on intent before authoring; the diff gate rules on the itemized delta
before anything lands. Consent binds to mutation.

**Approve → canonize --apply** — the approval freezes the proposal by
hash; the apply replays exactly that changeset: verify everything
before writing anything, re-derive the machine layer, re-export the
backup, chain the event log.

**Event log & inverse** — one chained, tamper-evident line per applied
round, with the delta's executable inverse recorded — every round can
be walked back.

**Stitch** — the same-round-endpoints mechanism: ground edges whose
target is born by this round's own schema edit ride a declared stitch
file, covered by the same approval, landing after re-derivation births
their endpoints.

**Rederive** — schema-bootstrap maintenance: recompute the machine
layer against the current schema, refusing if ground would change.

**Sitting** — an owner session that rules on a collated sheet of
questions in one pass, rule-by-exception welcome.

**Opening move** — every round's first duty: pay the previous round's
debts (stamp its PR onto its Judgment rows, land its deferred edges).

### The Judgment stratum

**Question / Decision / Answer / Opinion / Requirement / TODO** — the
kernel's ruling vocabulary, all citizens: something open; a ruling made
(by whom, when — supersession expected); a clarification; an agent's
judgment with confidence (junior until ratified); a binding constraint;
work pending. **Approved Omission / Approved Difference** — editorial
rulings the parity judge consults: this absence (or this changed
rendering) is approved and passes forever. **Verbatim** — a passage
pinned to carry word-for-word; the stored bytes are the truth, the
normalized form is only a matching key.

### Quality machinery

**Parity** — the regeneration bar, owner-ruled: nothing lost, nothing
invented, nothing distorted; presentation free. The **judge** compares
claims mechanically and returns verdicts (matched, omitted, invented,
distorted); reds name themselves.

**Attribution** — the other half of the triangle: every claim in a
draft must find its home in canon. **Parity proves draft ≡ original;
attribution proves draft ⊆ canon** — and a claim that passes parity
but has no home is a hole in *canon*, found automatically.

**The ladder (rungs)** — how strong a claim's home is: **first-class**
(a citizen's structured properties, edges, or Step lifts carry the
fact), **receipt** (found in a citizen's carried sentence quotes),
**soup / prose-only** (found only inside long prose — an honest home
AND a named debt). The rung rides the verdict as its confidence.

**Census** — decomposing an artifact into claims and attributing every
one. **Fact grain** — the ruled claim size: one atomic assertion
("Mary gave Arthur an apple" is three claims).

**Soup map** — the census's output read as a debt map: which sections'
facts are structured citizens and which still live as prose blobs.
The prioritized worklist for ingestion.

**Gap vs. invention** — a homeless claim splits on parity: the
original says it → canon gap (a debt; shipping never stops); parity
called it invented → a named red, presented with the artifact, never
hidden. **Phantom gap** — a "gap" the matcher couldn't see was already
home; **laundering** is removing phantoms from the worklist by reading
structure, not just text.

**Corpus** — the ledger of floors (`graph/corpus/floors.jsonl`) plus
the command that re-checks them all; a deleted guard reds as "the
guard is gone," naming the approval it orphaned.

**Tripwire** — a test that exists to refuse a specific forgetting: the
schema-version ledger, the roster check, the vocabulary leak. When a
tripwire reds, it worked.

### Runs and margins

**Run / trace** — one casting of agents against a brief, its record
kept as a run-scoped judgment graph: who was cast, what they were
told, what they consulted, what they judged. Claims about runs cite
traces; recollection is not a source.

**Margin** — the system's own annotations on an artifact, span-anchored
(the quote re-locates if the text moves): low-confidence calls,
uncertainties, questions. The owner replies in the same margin; the
reply threads to the Opinion it answers.

**Earned citation** — strong-form attribution: a citation counts when
the cited citizen appears in the drafter's trace. Right-answer-wrong-
path re-derives invisibly.

**Park, never die** — a blocked or interrupted run keeps its state and
resumes; the owner never has to say "try again."

### Lenses — who sees what

**Visibility Class** — a named set of graph elements; the only unit
permissions speak about. Kind **knowledge** (assume-deny: hidden
unless granted) or **masking** (assume-allow: removed only when a mask
names it).

**Visibility Group** — a subject of sight; individuals are size-1
groups; groups nest. (Named "Visibility Group" because a knowledge
base may need the plain word "Group" for its own domain.)

**Verdict** — an authored ALLOWED or DENIED between a group and a
class; denies target flat classes only.

**Fold / lens** — the fold is a subject's transitive group set; the
lens is that fold compiled into what they may see, enforced on the
in-memory graph itself so edges never dangle and derived layers
recompute under it. **Activation** — wearing a subset of your groups
this session; exiting a Pocket is a lens subtraction, not a
membership edit.

**Super admin** — no lens applied. Not a subject with every grant — the
absence of filtering.

**Redacted refusal** — the subject-facing answer for anything hidden:
one uniform "Nothing by that name that you can see." Candid
explanations are a curator privilege.

**Sealed reading** — intake's first phase: comprehend the artifact on
its own terms (kernel allowed, project canon forbidden) before any
mapping, so canon can't bias the reading. **Mapping phase** — then
each artifact-local claim is judged against canon: same-as / extends /
new / contradicts, every mapping a recorded Opinion.

### Campaign terms

**Re-ingest** — the declared milestone: rebuild canon clean from the
published knowledge base, rulings carried, the census as the ruler.

**Succession** — the original remains the parity reference until
the owner *explicitly* declares otherwise. No milestone implies it.

**Wave** — one gated slice of a campaign, sized by the worklist,
closed at a diff gate.

storybook project need it?" Semver'd; changes are **ceremonies**.

schema: its labels, catalogs, relationships — living ON the graph as
the Archetype stratum. Owner-governed, versioned as a plain revision
number. The from-sources

bootstrap files are git archaeology.

owner ruling, a Decision row naming it, the version bump and ledger

**schema ceremony** is its project-layer sibling: a closed list of
permitted change classes riding an ordinary gated round, itemized in the delta
report's marked section — approving that round IS the ruling.

layer starts empty and grows through gated rounds.

project layer: a new spec-carrying label arriving with its
declaration, permitted only while nothing yet sits underneath it.

gates → apply. Nothing reaches canon any other way.

freely. Wiped and re-cut per round; mistakes here cost nothing.

**Base pin** — cutting scratch records canon's content identity. If
canon moves mid-round, the apply refuses by name — no round lands on a
base that shifted under it.

declared base (schema-only for a rebuild line; clone-of-canon for a
pocket), with its own authoring
copy, ceremony, and chained log, physically unable to write the KB's
live canon, adopted only by the owner's succession ceremony — never a
flag. Pinned base + delta is the contract; the clone is an
implementation detail. A **Pocket Universe ("Pocket")** is a branch
cut as a clone of canon and declared a pocket; its work returns
through merge, prepared as the target's ordinary gated round. The
world-level correlation of pockets — one per member KB the work
mutates, read-pins for the rest, landing at one collated gate with
verify-all-before-apply-any extended across every member KB — is
the designed next rung.

linted (machine layers refuse authorship), rendered as a report. Its
content hash IS the proposal's identity.

on intent before authoring; the diff gate rules on the itemized delta
before anything lands. Consent binds to mutation.

backup, chain the event log.

round, with the delta's executable inverse recorded — every round can
be walked back.

target is born by this round's own schema edit ride a declared stitch

layer against the current schema, refusing if ground would change.

draft must find its home in canon. **Parity proves draft ≡ original;

fact), **receipt** (found in a citizen's carried sentence quotes),

the owner *explicitly* declares otherwise. No milestone implies it.

**Wave** — one gated slice of a campaign, sized by the worklist,
closed at a diff gate.

    Approved --> Draft : preconditions violated — rework against moved base
    Applied --> Superseded : a later delta revises these facts
    Applied --> Reverted : inverse applied (only while nothing built on it)
    Superseded --> [*]
    Reverted --> [*]

        entry. Temporality for free.

under the knowledge base's own custody.

permissions own only branch readability, and everything about what is
visible WITHIN a graph belongs to the lens layer, enforced on the
in-memory graph value — never to Neo4j privileges.

citizen in its schema edit cannot author ground edges pointing at it in
scratch (scratch is cut pre-schema, so the endpoint does not exist to
point at). Those edges ride the round's stitch file

## The narrative: you hand the agent a doc with a table

Running example: `sources/03-the-hollow-wood.md` arrives, containing a
Beasts table. "Let's intake this."

### Phase 1 — Recon

**What you experience:** nothing yet. The agent reads quietly for a minute.

**Under the hood:** the agent reads the doc cold and identifies, by
**semantic comprehension**, every entity, relationship, and rule the
content asserts — regardless of casing or formatting discipline (not
everyone capitalizes their terms; identification is reasoning about
meaning, never a word search). Pronouns and other indirect references get
special attention — "they pass it to their thing" requires resolving who
*they* is and what *it* refers to — so recon may take **multiple
disambiguation passes**, and a reference that stays genuinely ambiguous

## The reading room (comprehension graph)

*Designer ruling (recorded as the canon-is-the-knowledge Decision row).*

**Canon is the knowledge.** The canonical graph holds Concepts and
Judgments, plus thin provenance anchors. A dumped artifact's *insides* —
its section tree, bodies, order, heading hierarchy, embedded-table
references — are the machine's understanding of the artifact, and they
live in the **comprehension graph**: a separate workspace the pipeline
builds per intake round (`python -m graph comprehend <artifact>`).

The lifecycle is **build → archive → dispose**:

- **Build** — one well-known workspace database (`comprehension`), wiped
  per round like scratch. Never a standing database per asset.
- **Archive** — at round close the room serializes to small flat files
  under `graph/comprehension/<name>-<fingerprint12>/` (kept with the
  record, like `graph/export/`). Any set of archives batch-imports back into the room
  (`--recall`) for browsing; rounds coexist because every citizen
  carries its artifact's fingerprint.
- **Dispose** — the live room is wiped (`--dispose`); the archives are
  the record.

**Canon's side of the line** (the thinning): canon keeps one thin
anchor per artifact — the citizen, carrying a content-hash
`fingerprint` — and citations are **artifact + span**: a procedure's
`specified_in` names `{artifact, section, approved_hash}` and is
verified against the file's bytes directly; the SPECIFIED_IN edge lands
on the Artifact with the section as edge detail. No section citizens,
no mentions index on canon (the room's assertions layer is the
successor; until it lands, "which sections discuss X" is answered by
text search).

This thinning is the rule for a canon that is ABOUT a domain — where
a dropped artifact is *evidence for* the knowledge, not the knowledge
itself. A corpus whose prose IS the knowledge — its records carried as
citizens, sections with verbatim bodies on the graph — inverts the
rule by design: there the sections are canon, and once the prose lives
on the graph there is no separate source left to anchor to
([engine-as-corpus.md](engine-as-corpus.md)).

**Identity rules.** An artifact's identity is the sha256 of its bytes —
one collaborator's `Downloads` copy and another's `Temp` copy are the
same artifact; paths and titles are display metadata. Sections carry
machine-internal ids derived from fingerprint + structural position
("3f2a9c1d4e5b:2.0.1") — deterministic, so a deleted archive's structure
recomputes bit-identical from the immutable bytes. Quirks inside a
dumped artifact (duplicate headings, skipped levels) are the pipeline's
job to absorb silently — never a submitter-facing warning. Canon-side
references (procedure citations, receipts) use fingerprint + span, never
comprehension ids, so canon integrity survives total archive loss.

**Content classes.** Every span of every section is classified so
the round-trip harness can dispatch it to the right renderer and judging
bar: `table` ({{csv:}} embeds), `procedure` (sections cited by a
procedure's specified_in), `rule-prose` (the default — the machine never
guesses flavor), and `verbatim-carried` (flavor text, approver-assigned
at the plan gate, never deduced). The **carried fraction** — how much
prose is carried verbatim — is the honesty valve's metric, reported per
artifact so "just store it verbatim" cannot silently become the whole
round-trip proof; the ceiling is approver-set and enforced by the
harness.

**The parity harness** consumes the classes: `python -m graph
roundtrip --scope <artifact> --draft <regeneration>` judges a draft at
the functional-parity bar — chapter scope, never section-by-section
(structure is free): tables at cell-level content equivalence with row
integrity, procedures against the approved programs' atoms (answer keys
add behavior teeth), prose through the claim-diff judge,
approved flavor byte-intact, inventions checked once against the
combined original corpus. One scorecard, every red named, exit nonzero —
no human in the comparison step. The cold draft itself is produced by
the fenced regeneration loop; the harness only judges.

The plan gate reads its structure view from the room; the assertions and
canon-impact layers of comprehension join with the first intake round
that runs through it.

# Two Ontology Layers

<!-- Engine-owned doctrine. Travels with the engine (like metaontology.yaml).
     Consuming knowledge bases import this into their agent instructions so it is
     standing context for ALL work, not an on-demand procedure. -->

The graph schema has two layers with different ownership and change ceremony:

- **Engine metaontology** (`graph/metaontology.yaml`): the project-agnostic
  kernel — the `Archetype` label, `INSTANCE_OF`, the four roots (**Concept**,
  **Facet**, **Provenance**, **Judgment**), and the common facet library
  (Ordered, Exclusive, Stateful, ...). The membership test: *would a kid's
  storybook project need it?* Changes here are cross-project design decisions
  of the highest weight — never made casually, never as a silent side effect
  of intake, always via explicit design dialogue with the owner. That
  dialogue may happen at a round's gate: a kernel ceremony may be declared
  and ruled mid-round when the round's evidence demands it, including a
  conditionally pre-authorized enabling engine change ("only on a real
  refusal, with its own tests"). What makes it a ceremony is the explicit
  owner ruling, a Decision row naming it, and the semver bump + ledger line
  riding the same change set — the dialogue and the record, not the
  calendar.
  A canon's committed backup embeds the kernel stratum it was
  built with, so the ceremony's change set also migrates every
  canon the engine repo ships (`python -m graph kernel-migrate`)
  — and a consuming knowledge base runs the same migration when
  it adopts the new engine: mutating commands refuse on the skew
  until it does.
  The splice keeps the world's own knowledge: the kernel wins every
  key it defines, and any enrichment a canon has laid on a kernel
  citizen beyond that rides the migration unchanged — named in the
  report, never silently dropped.

- **Project ontology** (the graph's own schema stratum): everything
  THIS knowledge base derived — its domain concepts, labels, catalogs,
  relationships, project-specific facets. Since the schema inversion the
  schema lives ON THE GRAPH as ground citizens — the Archetype
  stratum, read by `ontology_from_graph` — and this is the owner's
  daily surface, following the ontology-has-one-owner rules.
  The from-sources era is closed: every knowledge base is born graph-native or ingested through the front door, and an early corpus's bootstrap files are archaeology
  in the project's own history, never a provenance surface. It versions from the
  event-log sequence, auto-stamped on the graph's Ontology anchor at
  apply, with an optional free-text `tag` beside it — semver stays with the kernel, whose bumps are ceremony (owner ruling).
  Three spec fields keep their stories here: `values:` on an ordered
  concept is the ladder's declared order, read when the schema
  stratum is seeded or migrated; `reader:` is a label's lift
  declaration — how its citizens' bodies and sections are read —
  guarded at derivation, which refuses an unknown kind by name; and
  a citizen born by reference under a declared `implicit:` label is
  itemized at the gate, never silent.
  Schema changes ride the SCHEMA CEREMONY: an ordinary owner-gated round may add a new declared concept, birth a new label (a spec-carrying row with nothing yet underneath it), edit a schema row's doc text, add an alias to a label's spec (a new surface spelling reading as an existing citizen — additions only), edit a label's render mapping (the table layout it renders through — add, change, or remove; the loader never reads it, so nothing moves), release a label's source registration (a program label's files leave once every citizen carries its own body and cites no file; any other label's source rows leave as archaeology no verb reads), declare a taxonomy link (an authored kind-of connection into a concept, both citizens existing), adopt the knowledge base's own declared name on its anchor (KB NAMED — identity may change hands at a gate, never quietly vanish), or remove an unreferenced schema row — itemized under the delta report's marked ceremony section, whose approval IS the ceremony ruling. A round may also declare moves — a rename of the world's own label or concept, or a re-homing of named citizens under a kind of what they were — itemized and guarded at the same gate, the approval covering them. Changes to an existing label or spec move data underneath them and stay refused: they ride the migration charter.

  Schema changes ride the SCHEMA CEREMONY: an ordinary owner-gated round may add a new declared concept, birth a new label (a spec-carrying row with nothing yet underneath it), edit a schema row's doc text, add an alias to a label's spec (a new surface spelling reading as an existing citizen — additions only), edit a label's render mapping (the table layout it renders through — add, change, or remove; the loader never reads it, so nothing moves), release a label's source registration (a program label's files leave once every citizen carries its own body and cites no file; any other label's source rows leave as archaeology no verb reads), declare a taxonomy link (an authored kind-of connection into a concept, both citizens existing), adopt the knowledge base's own declared name on its anchor (KB NAMED — identity may change hands at a gate, never quietly vanish), or remove an unreferenced schema row — itemized under the delta report's marked ceremony section, whose approval IS the ceremony ruling. A round may also declare moves — a rename of the world's own label or concept, or a re-homing of named citizens under a kind of what they were — itemized and guarded at the same gate, the approval covering them. Changes to an existing label or spec move data underneath them and stay refused: they ride the migration charter.
